scholarships.title: Whitley Awards 2027
scholarships.degree: Not applicable - professional project award, no degree awarded

eligibility: Grassroots conservation leaders who are nationals of the country where they work (born there, or having lived there long term and obtained national status) and are embedded in local communities

Work based in at least one eligible country - countries not classified as a High-Income Economy by the World Bank, with some exceptions based on WFN's funding history; the full list of eligible countries is published by WFN

Wildlife conservation projects delivering measurable positive impacts for threatened ecosystems and biodiversity at the landscape or seascape level, while providing tangible benefits to Indigenous peoples and local communities
Applicants who work for a locally incorporated NGO, charity, not for profit, or university
Strong communicators who inspire others and collaborate effectively and share their learnings and results
Applicants must be able to communicate in English, verbally without a translator (total fluency not required)

Leadership and teamwork - individuals must be backed by an experienced team or organisation that can demonstrate past success and an evidence-based approach; individuals working in isolation are not eligible
Ecosystem-level projects are preferred; genuine flagship species projects are accepted but not if results are purely species-specific
Community-led conservation projects are encouraged, and all projects must demonstrate how they empower, engage and benefit the Indigenous peoples and communities with which they work
Grassroots, pragmatic conservation work that is realistic but ambitious, replicable or scalable
Actions that will have clear, measurable outcomes, with careful consideration of the indicators used to evidence impact
Sustainable projects that will continue well beyond the Whitley Award, demonstrating long-term planning
Projects that demonstrate value for money and an ability to manage funding at the Whitley Award level (GBP 50,000)
Projects for which a Whitley Award will make a significant difference; priority to applicants who can clearly demonstrate need
Work that would benefit from greater visibility, particularly projects that could gain momentum through media exposure and wider recognition
No invitation or nomination is needed to apply
existing.eligibility_summary: Grassroots conservation leaders who are nationals of the country where they work, are embedded in local communities, are backed by an experienced team or organisation, and work for a locally incorporated NGO, charity, not-for-profit or university, on a wildlife conservation project delivering measurable positive impacts for threatened ecosystems and biodiversity at landscape or seascape level in at least one eligible country (not a World Bank High-Income Economy, with WFN exceptions).
benefits: GBP 50,000 in project funding over one year

Membership of a global community of more than 230 conservation leaders working across over 80 countries

existing.english_requirement: Applicants must be able to communicate in English. Total fluency is not required, but applicants must be able to communicate verbally in English without a translator, so that winners can take part fully in the Whitley Awards week involving interviews, networking events, training and media opportunities.
application_method: Check your eligibility against the published criteria and the full list of eligible countries
Register for a WFN account through the online application portal at https://wfn.eformsolutions.com/
Log in to the portal and complete the application form online, saving as you go
Download the Microsoft Word logical framework/timeline template and the Microsoft Excel budget template from the portal
Complete both templates in your own time and upload the finished versions to the portal
Nominate three referees and make sure they submit their references before the deadline
Submit your application before 23:59 GMT on Friday, 30 October 2026
existing.selection_notes: WFN publishes what it looks for rather than a scoring formula: strong communicators who collaborate and share learning; leadership and teamwork backed by an experienced organisation with an evidence-based approach; ecosystem-level projects (genuine flagship species projects accepted but not if results are purely species-specific); community-led projects that empower, engage and benefit Indigenous peoples and communities; pragmatic work that is realistic but ambitious and replicable or scalable; clear measurable outcomes with considered indicators; sustainability beyond the award with long-term planning; value for money and ability to manage GBP 50,000 of funding; a project to which the award will make a significant difference, with priority to demonstrated need; and work that would benefit from greater visibility. Practical process gates: three referees must be nominated and must submit their references by the deadline (the applicant's responsibility), and applications on out-of-date templates from previous years will not be considered. Winners are announced at the Whitley Awards Ceremony in London in Spring 2027.
existing.best_fit: Mid-career grassroots conservation leaders who are nationals of the country where they work, work for a locally incorporated NGO, charity, not-for-profit or university, are backed by an experienced team, and are running a proven, measurable, ecosystem-level conservation project in an eligible country that is ready to scale.
existing.notes: No invitation or nomination is required to apply. MSc or PhD fieldwork is not funded, and pure academic research, expeditions, start-up or pilot projects, joint or team entries, applications submitted on behalf of someone else, one-person operations, land purchases, building construction, captive animal welfare and rehabilitation, and general government employees are all excluded. Applicants employed by government-funded universities are typically eligible. Applicants must be able to communicate verbally in English without a translator. Templates are updated annually and out-of-date forms are not considered. It is the applicant's responsibility to ensure their three referees submit references by the deadline. No deferral, renewal, return-home or clinical-restriction rules are published on the pages read.
existing.duration: Each Whitley Award is worth GBP 50,000 in project funding over one year. Winners are announced at the annual Whitley Awards Ceremony in London in Spring 2027.
existing.application_period: Applications for the 2027 Whitley Awards are open and close at 23:59 GMT on Friday, 30 October 2026. Registered applicants can log in to the WFN application portal and complete the form at any time before the deadline. Winners will be announced during the annual Whitley Awards Ceremony in London in Spring 2027.
